findings.title: Duplicate datasources for https://127.0.0.1:9200|[wazuh-alerts-4.x-]YYYY.MM.DD
findings.detail: Blue Cloud Dashboard (cftkburm1y9z4f), Threat Detection Dashboard (ffu1imxcwterkc) all point at the same OpenSearch cluster and index pattern.
findings.fix: Consolidate to one datasource, or keep one canonical id per index pattern and re-point every panel at it so imports are deterministic.

findings.title: Duplicate datasources for https://127.0.0.1:9200|
findings.detail: grafana-opensearch-datasource (aftnm572lwhz4f), grafana-opensearch-datasource-1 (ffu5g832pmn7ka) all point at the same OpenSearch cluster and index pattern.

findings.title: No MITRE field referenced
findings.detail: DoD requires the MITRE view to be populated from real alerts, but no panel queries a rule.mitre.* field.
findings.fix: Add a terms aggregation on rule.mitre.id / rule.mitre.technique / rule.mitre.tactic.

findings.title: Datasource "Blue Cloud Dashboard" declares version 2.0.0, cluster is 7.10.2
findings.detail: The datasource jsonData.version drives how the plugin builds date_histogram intervals and index patterns. Declaring 2.0.0 against a 7.10.2 cluster can silently produce empty or malformed aggregations.
findings.fix: Set the datasource version to 7.10.2, or use a plain wildcard index name so no version-dependent interpolation is needed.

findings.title: Datasource "Blue Cloud Dashboard" uses the bracketed legacy index pattern
findings.detail: Index name "[wazuh-alerts-4.x-]YYYY.MM.DD" is the ES 1.x/2.x style template. The plugin's frontend path expands it correctly, but the backend path (POST /api/ds/query) does not resolve it the same way - every panel replayed through the Grafana API returns zero frames.
findings.fix: Use the plain wildcard form "wazuh-alerts-4.x-*" with interval "No pattern". It resolves identically in both paths and removes the ambiguity.

findings.title: No level 15+ alerts in the last 24h
findings.detail: Highest rule.level observed in the last 24h is 12 (3:2638125, 4:23092, 5:208847, 6:119446, 7:99, 8:23, 9:348, 10:73, 12:14). The "Critical Alerts" gauge (rule.level >= 15) and the critical band of the severity panels therefore always read zero in this window.
findings.fix: Either widen the default time range of the severity panels, lower the critical threshold to match the data the lab actually produces, or label the gauge explicitly as "no critical alerts in window" so an analyst does not read it as a broken panel.

findings.title: No auto-refresh interval
findings.detail: refresh is empty; panels only update on manual reload.
findings.fix: Set refresh to e.g. "1m" for SOC dashboards so analysts do not stare at stale numbers.

findings.title: No tags
findings.detail: Untagged dashboards are harder to find via /api/search and harder to group in the UI.
findings.fix: Tag with e.g. ["wazuh","soc","<domain>"] consistently across the set.

findings.title: Dashboard lives in the General folder
findings.detail: All six dashboards sit at the org root rather than a dedicated folder.
findings.fix: Group them in a folder (e.g. "SOC Detection Lab") so they can be exported/imported as one unit.

findings.title: MITRE view scope
findings.detail: MITRE panels are restricted to: MITRE ATT&CK Heat Map: rule.groups:suricata AND rule.mitre.id:*. Rules outside that filter are not represented in the heat map.
findings.fix: Widen the query (drop the rule.groups filter) if the heat map is meant to cover every alert, or state the scope in the panel title.

findings.title: Datasource "Blue Cloud Dashboard" has PPL enabled
findings.detail: The panels in this set are authored with Lucene query syntax (queryType: lucene). PPL is available but unused; the PPL endpoint on this cluster does not accept hyphenated index names unquoted, so switching a panel to PPL needs care.
findings.fix: Leave PPL off for this dashboard set, or document the PPL syntax separately.
